name: Build From Suffixes
description: You are given an integer $$$n$$$ and a sequence $$$a$$$ of $$$n-1$$$ integers, each element is either $$$0$$$ or $$$1$$$. You are asked to build a string of length $$$n$$$ such that: each letter is one of " abcd "; if $$$a_i=1$$$, then the $$$i$$$-th suffix of the string is lexicographically smaller than the $$$(i+1)$$$-th suffix; if $$$a_i=0$$$, then the $$$i$$$-th suffix of the string is lexicographically greater than the $$$(i+1)$$$-th suffix. You will be asked $$$q$$$ queries of form: $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le n - 1$$$) — flip the value of $$$a_i$$$ (if $$$a_i=0$$$, then set $$$a_i$$$ to $$$1$$$, and vice versa). After each query print the number of different strings that satisfy the given constraints modulo $$$998\,244\,353$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 10^5$$$; $$$1 \le q \le 10^5$$$) — the length of the string and the number of queries. The second line contains $$$n-1$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{n-1}$$$ ($$$a_i \in \{0, 1\}$$$) — the constraints on suffixes of the string. Each of the next $$$q$$$ lines contains a query: an integer $$$i$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le n - 1$$$) — flip the value of $$$a_i$$$ (if $$$a_i=0$$$, then set $$$a_i$$$ to $$$1$$$, and vice versa).
output_specification: After each query print the number of different strings that satisfy the given constraints modulo $$$998\,244\,353$$$.
approach_summary: Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to N using Fermat's Little Theorem (mod 10^9+7 or 998244353). Answer nCr queries in O(1) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1488H — Build From Suffixes [310. Large Factorials and Binomial Coefficients]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Combinatorial selection $\binom{N}{K} = \frac{N!}{K!(N-K)!} \pmod P$ can be evaluated in $O(1)$ by precomputing factorials $fact[i] = fact[i-1] \cdot i \pmod P$ and inverse factorials $invFact[i] = invFact[i+1] \cdot (i+1) \pmod P$ using Fermat's Little Theorem $a^{P-2} \equiv a^{-1} \pmod P$.
